claims.value: refused a dice-game and marked himself rather than pay
claims.quote: People thought scars were plain things; Nasir had given a story for this one once, when the drink had been bitter and the night long: he had walked away from a dice-game rather than pay a debt he had not earned, and had marked himself instead to keep the ledger straight in his head.

claims.quote: Using a dented measure he had kept for years, he dipped, leveled the rim and wiped a drop back into the tin with the heel of his hand. "We can't be bleeding stores in port," he said, more to the figures than to Amina.

He traced the knots on the sheet's reefing line with his thumb as he worked—an old helmsman's habit that smoothed his hands and his temper—and hummed a thin lullaby under his breath. He threaded the needle with a small curse and stitched the ragged edge down into a straight seam, eyes half on the cloth and half on Amina.

claims.value: The scrap had a looped mark near its corner that he said 'leans toward memory'.
claims.quote: Tariq balanced on the rail with a scrap of yellowed paper spread on his palm, ink flaking along its tear. The scrap had been the kind of thing he kept tucked away; the rest of his books lived beneath a loose plank in the forecastle, wrapped in oilcloth against salt. He smoothed the paper and pointed to a looped mark near its corner. "This one leans toward memory," he said, his voice careful.

She let the map rest beneath her hand, its paper warm from her shirt.

claims.value: token kept beneath her kerchief at throat
claims.quote: They gave me a map and this," and she tapped the silver disc beneath her kerchief.
